name: Pavonine
lede: Pavonine is an old word for the colors of a peacock: iridescent greenish blue; the Maerz and Paul color dictionary used it for a dull blue.

sections.title: The peacock's word
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines pavonine as iridescent, of the peacock in color or character, and greenish blue, and lists pavonazzo with the meaning peacock-coloured, greenish blue [1]. Maerz and Paul recorded Pavonine as a color name in 1930, with a first record in 1688 [2].

The swatch is not what the dictionary describes. It is a dull denim blue, with hue near 250 on the CIELAB wheel, well away from a greenish blue [2]. Its nearest named color is [[dark-orient-blue]], and [[denim]] is only 5.4 units away [2]. For the real peacock color, see [[peacock-blue]] and [[teal]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of the swatch covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 114 [3]. It is often a mid-tone, and it is about 3.2 times as common in the 1900s as across the archive [3]. Monet's [[painting:aic-16568|Water Lilies]] of 1906 carries it over about 41 per cent of the picture [3]. Another near match is Van Gogh's 1889 self-portrait [3]. The most common company in these paintings is the word denim [3]. As photographed: museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings; a color match is not a pigment test.

origin.source: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour; Maerz & Paul
